messages:
sam: Heads-up — noticing a slow, rolling increase in preemptible evictions across us-central GPU pools over the last 15m. p50 token latency +30ms, p99 +120ms, kv-cache miss rate up ~9%. Looks like mixed-pool churn rather than full AZ outage.
ishaan: On it. Do we have a spike in batching latency or just backend pod reschedules?
sam: Mostly reschedules. Logs show a flurry of node term signals + kubelet draining around 1865431950..1865432040. Batching latency ticked when replicas dropped below steady-state for a few routes.
maria: Can we flip routing to prefer dedicated/on-demand for the affected model tags while we stabilize? We have spare reserved capacity in us-central-1-d.
ryan: Cost note: moving traffic to dedicated will run ~ $1.1k/day extra if sustained for 24h for the volumes we're seeing. ok for incident window? :thinking_face:
ishaan: Yes for now. Prioritize availability. I'll kick a scale and routing override.
ishaan: Running -> ./infra scale-dedicated --region us-central --pool infer-dedicated-a --delta +4  (expect ~2m to attach)
infra-bot: scheduler request accepted — scaling infer-dedicated-a +4 GPUs. ETA 3m. job_id=scale-1865432123
sam: Also enabling temporary routing override: set route_override: {model_tag: "prod-v2", prefer_on_demand: true, ttl: 15m} — will push in 2m.
maria: Suggest we also tighten autoscaler cooldown to avoid flapping: set min_ready_seconds=120 and stabilization_window=300s for mixed pools. That should reduce churn when spot supply blips.
ryan: Agreed. Also lower max_batch_size from 128 -> 96 for the affected routes while on-demand ramp to reduce p99.
ishaan: Applied routing override and batch cap change. Command: kubectl patch cm routing-overrides -n redwood --patch '{"data":{"prod-v2":"prefer_on_demand=true;max_batch=96"}}'
infra-bot: Config patch acknowledged. Rolling update to routing-config. commit=7a1f9b3
scheduler-bot: Dedicated pool infer-dedicated-a scaled to +4 GPUs (attached). new_capacity=28/32.
sam: Early signal: p99 down ~70ms (from +120), kv-cache miss trending down. eviction rate still elevated but less consumer impact.
maria: Recommend we leave override for 15m and then evaluate. If evictions persist, we should automate detection -> auto-fallback to dedicated for 5m to avoid manual ops.
ryan: Opening follow-up ticket to evaluate fallback automation and cost/cooldown knobs: INF-4123. Assigning to eng-infra + infra-ml for batching interplay.
ishaan: FYI I'll also add a temporary alert threshold: if node-drain-rate > 3/min across a region, trigger routing override automatically.
sam: Sounds good. Thanks all — keep updates here.
infra-bot: Metrics back to baseline at 1865432945. p99 within normal range. Eviction rate decaying.
ryan: Closing immediate incident; will track INF-4123 for long-term improvements. :white_check_mark:
maria: Postmortem note: consider reducing spot ratio for critical low-latency models by default, add a canary for routing override during peak hours.
sam: Agreed — will draft short runbook change and post in #eng-infra-runbooks. End of thread.
